title: Multi-Channel LFP Denoising: NP1 vs NP2
text:
Seven simultaneous NP1+NP2 recordings (datasets 001–007) were collected by Kim in the Steinmetz lab to characterise how probe version and referencing scheme affect LFP quality. NP2 was recorded with three referencing conditions (external, tip reference, join tip references) at two cortical depths (high/low), controlled by the NP2 channel mapping; NP1 always used external referencing.
The datasets with matched external referencing (004, 005) provide a ground-truth convergence test: effective denoising should bring the NP1 and NP2 CSD distributions closer together.

title: Multi-Channel LFP Denoising: NP1 vs NP2
text:
Conclusions

Voltage amplitude is equivalent between NP1 and NP2 when the same external referencing scheme is applied, once hardware filters are accounted for.
CAR can´t be applied on both NP1 and NP2, the NP2 spatial span is much shorter than NP1, resulting in a destructive effect.
First order CSD conserves a small amount of correlation, while second order CSD destroys it completely. Spatial noise attenuation slightly improves on the correlation after spatial derivative.

title: Multi-Channel LFP Denoising: NP1 vs NP2
text:
Probe geometry
NP1 has 384 channels in a checkerboard pattern (two interleaved columns); NP2.4 has 96 channels arranged in four straight columns on a single shank. In experiments 1-4 the lower channels of NP2 recorded. Then for experiments 5-7, NP2 was driven down and higher channels were selected to be recorded.



Matched channel locations for datasets 004 (left) and 005 (right). NP1 channels (blue) and the depth-aligned NP2 channels (orange) are overlaid on a common y-axis.

title: Multi-Channel LFP Denoising: NP1 vs NP2
text:
Preprocessing - Cross-correlation Evaluation
The evaluation metric is the peak of the normalised cross-correlation between matched NP1/NP2 channel pairs. Each raw snippet goes through the following ordered stages:



Stage
Description




bandpass
0.2-300Hz bandpass filter (includes sample shifts)


car
Global CAR subtracted from bandpass


cadzow
Spatiotemporal SVD denoising (rank 4, fmax 200 Hz)


csd1
1st-order finite-difference CSD on bandpass


csd1_denoise
1st-order CSD on cadzow


csd2
2nd-order CSD on bandpass


csd2_denoise
2nd-order CSD on cadzow






Signal traces and normalised cross-correlogram for dataset 004. Each row is one preprocessing stage; right panels show the xcorr within ±200 ms.





Same for dataset 005.

title: Ephys-Atlas Region Boundary Landmarks
text:
Beyond the atlas itself it is useful to supply the community with a set of anatomical landmarks: locations in the brain where there is a sharp transition in predicted electrophysiological features that a scientist can use to confirm or refine their probe location. The DG–thalamus LFP landmark from the repro-ephys paper (eLife 2024) is one such example.
The strategy here is a brute-force search:

For each region boundary at the Cosmos level (13 regions), collect all probe penetrations that cross it.
For each ephys feature, test whether there is a statistically significant and large-effect-size transition across the boundary.
Rank candidate landmarks by effect size / p-value and document them.

Vintage used: 2026_W21 (~383 k channels across all IBL recordings).

title: Ephys-Atlas Region Boundary Landmarks
text:
Cosmos boundary transition counts
Channels are first aggregated by depth (axial_um) within each probe — taking the modal Cosmos region at each depth level — before adjacent-depth transitions are detected. The matrix is directional: row = “from” region, column = “to” region.



13×13 directional transition count matrix at the Cosmos level. Diagonal is masked (grey). Color range is clipped at the 97th percentile of off-diagonal values.


The dominant transitions all pass through root (the catch-all outside-brain label), reflecting that most probes enter and exit the brain through unlabelled tissue. Biologically meaningful boundaries are off the root row/column: MB↔︎TH (98/51), CB↔︎root (248/338), HPF↔︎root (368/385), and Isocortex→root (44/435, strongly asymmetric as expected — probes enter cortex from above).
